panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A is a sagittal T2/STIR MRI showing intramedullary hyperintensity, consistent with the findings for acute spinal cord infarction. D: Panel D is the ADC map showing low signal, which confirms the restricted diffusion (isodensity) corresponding to the acute spinal cord infarction.

in_text_mentions: Spinal MRI, performed approximately 18 hours after symptom onset, demonstrated T2 hyperintensity and restricted diffusion involving the anterior horns of the spinal gray matter from T10-T11 to the conus medullaris at L1-L2, with corresponding low signal on the ADC map. These findings were consistent with acute spinal cord infarction in the anterior spinal artery territory (Figure 1). No adjacent vertebral body signal abnormality or traumatic lesion was identified.

Therefore, we made a diagnosis of spinal cord infarction manifesting as sulcal artery syndrome.
